specialRules.ruleFull: Roll a D6 at the start of each Night Goblin turn. On a 1 they squabble and do nothing else for the rest of the turn. Only Night Goblins are affected: trolls, squigs, snotlings and other non-goblins act as normal.
Night Goblins hate Dwarfs. No other greenskin of the warband is affected, and a Fanatic is too far gone to be affected either.
The warband may hire the Black Orc Bodyguard and Snerik, Night Goblin Scout.
Any model in the warband within 6" of the Big Boss may use his Leadership instead of his own.
The Shaman is a spell caster and uses Waaagh! Magic.
The Fanatic needs a steady supply of Mad Cap Mushrooms. If he has none before a battle he stays in his cave and takes no part. If he has them, he eats them before the battle.
The Fanatic is subject to frenzy, and must test for permanent damage after the battle as the mushrooms' rules say.
The Fanatic strikes first in combat, ignoring the penalties for weapons and the order of Initiative.

fighters.name: Cave Squig
fighters.equipment: None. Cave Squigs never use or need weapons or armour.

specialRules.ruleFull: A Cave Squig has no set Movement: roll 2D6 for the distance it moves. Squigs never run and never declare charges; instead they may touch an enemy model within that 2D6" move, and then count as charging for that round of close combat.

A Cave Squig must stay within 6" of a Night Goblin. If it has none within 6" at the start of its Movement phase it goes wild: from then on move it 2D6" in a random direction each of its Movement phases, and if that takes it into contact with any model, friend or foe, it fights that model as normal. It is out of the Night Goblin player's control for the rest of the game.
Cave Squigs are animals of a sort and gain no experience.
The warband may never hold more Cave Squigs than Night Goblins.

fighters.name: Troll
fighters.equipment: None. A Troll often carries a big club, but can never be given weapons or armour.

specialRules.ruleFull: A Troll causes fear.
A Troll is subject to stupidity.

Trolls have a unique physiology that allows them to regenerate wounds. Whenever an enemy successfully inflicts a wound on a Troll roll a D6, on a result of 4 or more the wound is ignored and the Troll is unhurt. Trolls may not regenerate wounds caused by fire or fire-based magic. Trolls never roll for Injury after a battle.
A Troll never learns a skill and gains no experience.

The warband must pay 15 gold crowns after every game to feed the Troll. With too little gold, the Big Boss may instead feed him three Snotlings or two Cave Squigs. If neither is paid, the Troll wanders off in search of food.
In place of his normal attacks, a Troll may be sick over one opponent in hand-to-hand combat: one attack that hits automatically at Strength 5 and allows no armour save.

fighters.name: Snotling
fighters.equipment: A pointy stick, which they find for themselves at no cost. It counts as a dagger and gives the enemy +1 to his armour save, or a 6+ save if he had none.

specialRules.ruleFull: Snotlings are bought as one mob of 5 for 50 gold crowns, and a lost member is replaced for 10 gold crowns, up to 5. They always move and fight as a mob: all members stay within 1" of each other and all join the same combat where they can.
A wounded Snotling is knocked down on a 1, stunned on a 2-3 and out of action on a 4-6.
A Snotling has a 6+ dodge save against shooting.

specialSkillsList.name: Ded Shooty
specialSkillsList.description: The clever little git adds +6" to the range of any missile weapons he uses (not including nets).

specialSkillsList.name: Sneaky Git (Karak Azgal)
specialSkillsList.description: Night Goblin Big Boss only. He may move D3 members of his warband after all other deployment is complete.

specialSkillsList.name: Netter (Karak Azgal)
specialSkillsList.description: The Goblin may declare a net charge and throw his net at the target as the rulebook says. If he hits and the target does not escape, the target counts as knocked down and the Goblin completes his charge; if he misses or the target escapes, it is a failed charge, and he stops 1" away if it would bring him into base contact. A warrior caught in a net is hit automatically in combat, though the Goblin still rolls to wound as against a knocked down enemy. In the warrior's next recovery phase, unless he is stunned or out of action, he cuts himself free, but may do nothing else and strikes last that turn, as if he had stood up from knocked down.

flags.what: The warband's minimum of 3 models is not imported: our templates hold no minimum.

Ded Shooty and Infiltrate ("As Skaven skill") are ours, name and effect; Infiltrate links our Infiltration. The PDF's Sneaky Git (move D3 warband members after deployment) and Netter (the 'chuck and charge' net charge) are not our skills of those names, so both are kept apart under the setting's name. See the decisions.
Sneaky Git is the Big Boss's alone, which opens its description.

Poison Daggers (25 gc, Common, Fanatics only), the Ball and Chain (15 gc, Common, Fanatics only) and Mad Cap Mushrooms (25 gc, Common) are ours at the PDF's prices, each a price row for this warband. Ours sells Mad Cap Mushrooms at 30+D3, Rare 9, which is unchanged.
The Ball and Chain's and Mad Cap Mushrooms' rules are "as Best of Town Cryer" and "as the rulebook", which ours carry; the Poison Daggers' printed rules match ours.
The Cave Squig's Movement is "2D6", kept as written. Its 0-5 count and "never more Cave Squigs than Night Goblins" are the count and the Cave Squigs rule on the fighter, which the app cannot check.
The Snotling Mob is 0-1 of 5 Snotlings for 50 gc, 10 gc each to replace: imported as a group of exactly 5 at 10 gc a model, with the Mob rule saying the rest.
The Mob rule prints "within 1\" (or 1/2\"?)": the 1" is taken and the author's query left out.
The Troll's profile is M6 WS3 BS1 S5 T4 W3 I1 A3 Ld4, as printed. His Regeneration is the Trolls' own rule, as our other Troll warbands hold it.
Starting experience: Big Boss 17, Shaman 10, Boss 6, Henchmen 0. Henchmen are bought in groups of 1-5, and no maximum is printed for the Night Goblins.
The Shaman "uses Waaagh! Magic as listed in Best of Town Cryer", read as our Waaaagh! Magic lore.
